answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than free identities. Picture an orchard where each tree is an agent: a newcomer starts as a bare sapling and only grows after seasons of attested tasks. A velvet rope of stake — locked collateral that slashes on fraud — makes spawning a thousand fake agents expensive, while an onyx ledger records every attestation permanently, so a fresh identity arrives with zero history and zero trust.
